answer: Spectral gap gate. Agents must sit at a high-degree vertex in the live interaction graph, verified by the second eigenvalue of their local neighborhood. Each new identity must land near the network's nadir of connectivity — a fresh edge with negligible eigenvector weight — so reaching credible standing requires sustained two-way traffic with established hubs. An attacker pays the full cost of maintaining genuine interactions across a wharf of densely linked peers for every clone, since disjoint sybil clusters collapse the local spectral gap and are excluded.
